title: Hims Big Game Commercial: “Sick of the System” (Super Bowl LIX, 2025)
ad_content: [00:00] Obesity is America's deadliest epidemic. [00:03] This is America. [00:04] 74% of us are overweight, [00:06] and obesity leads to half a million deaths each year. [00:09] - Well, you just have to stop eating, Jimmy. [00:11] This is America. [00:12] Something's broken, and it's not our bodies. [00:14] It's the system. [00:15] Welcome to weight loss in America-- [00:18] - Like and subscribe. [00:19] A $160 billion industry [00:20] that feeds on our failure. [00:23] There are medications that work, [00:25] but they're priced for profits, not patients. [00:27] This is America. [00:28] This system wasn't built to help us. [00:30] It was built to keep us sick and stuck. [00:33] But not anymore. [00:35] Hims & Hers offers life-changing weight loss medications. [00:38] They're affordable, doctor trusted, [00:41] and formulated in the USA. [00:43] You get a treatment plan designed by a doctor [00:46] to fit your body, goals, and lifestyle. [00:49] You deserve to feel great in your body. [00:51] This is the future of healthcare. [00:54] This is Hims & Hers. [00:56] Join us in the fight for a healthier America.

expected_findings.claim: Hims & Hers offers life-changing weight loss medications. They're affordable, doctor trusted, and formulated in the USA.
expected_findings.rule: 21 U.S.C. 352(n); 21 CFR 202.1(e)(1) (broadcast major statement); FTC Act §§5, 12

expected_findings.claim: Hims & Hers offers life-changing weight loss medications.
There are medications that work, but they're priced for profits, not patients. ... But not anymore. Hims & Hers offers life-changing weight loss medications. They're affordable
They're affordable, doctor trusted, and formulated in the USA. (on-screen supers: "doctor-trusted", "formulated in the USA")
Prescription required. Compounded drug products are not FDA approved. The FDA does not evaluate compounded drug products for safety, effectiveness, or quality.
expected_findings.rule: FTC Act §5 (clear and conspicuous; 16 CFR 255.0(f)); 21 CFR 202.1(e)(1)

expected_findings.claim: Not available in all 50 states. Weight Loss by Hims & Hers is a holistic program that includes nutrition support, technological tools, and medication kits including customized compounded medications or compounded GLP-1 injections, prescribed based on what your provider determines is medically appropriate for you. See website for details and important safety information.
expected_findings.rule: FTC Act §5 (clear and conspicuous; 16 CFR 255.0(f)); 21 CFR 202.1(e)(1)

must_not_flag: "74% of us are overweight, and obesity leads to half a million deaths each year" (00:04-00:10) - public-health statistics, not a product efficacy claim
No claim that the products are FDA-approved is made - do not raise false_fda_approval_claim
"You get a treatment plan designed by a doctor to fit your body, goals, and lifestyle" (00:43-00:49) - description of the telehealth service
The presence of a 'Prescription required' / 'Compounded drug products are not FDA approved' disclosure is correct; the problem is only its prominence and duration
notes: Provenance: official 'hims' YouTube channel, uploaded 2025-01-28; aired during Super Bowl LIX (Feb 9, 2025). Downloaded at 480p with yt-dlp; captions = uploader-provided English captions. Labels by agent from captions+frames; needs human confirmation. On-screen timing: compounded/not-FDA-approved super visible ~39.4-41.8s only (two lines, ~2% of frame height, white text over moving footage while the large super reads 'doctor-trusted'); end super ~57-60s is small, low-contrast white text on beige. Audio never says 'compounded' and gives no side effects. Visuals at ~24-27s show injection pens on a production line with chyron 'WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGMAKERS GRILLED OVER HIGH PRICES', which sets up the implied equivalence. Context: critics said the ad omits side effects and risks and that the product is not FDA-approved; Sens. Marshall and Durbin wrote to FDA; Partnership for Safe Medicines asked FDA and FOX to stop the ad (https://www.managedhealthcareexecutive.com/view/hims-and-hers-superbowl-ad-draws-controversy-over-safety). FDA later sent Hims & Hers a warning letter dated Sept 9, 2025 (posted Sept 16) about website claims that its compounded products have 'the same active ingredient' as Wegovy/Ozempic; the letter concerned the website, not this ad (https://spectrumlocalnews.com/us/snplus/health/2025/09/16/fda-takes-aim-at-hims---hers--weight-loss-drugs-in-ad-blitz). The two compounded_drug_misrepresentation findings may be merged by graders.

title: Serena Williams Super Bowl LX Commercial ‘Healthier on Ro’ (2026)
ad_content: [00:00] I'm on Ro. 34 lbs down on GLP-1s. [00:06] Healthier on Ro. Supported on Ro. [00:11] FDA approved GLP-1 options. Now even in a pill. [00:16] Weight loss expertise I trust. [00:18] I'm moving better on Ro. [00:21] I'm feeling better on Ro. [00:25] I'm Serena Williams. This is me on Ro.

expected_findings.claim: 34 lbs down on GLP-1s. ... FDA approved GLP-1 options. Now even in a pill. ... I'm moving better on Ro. I'm feeling better on Ro.
expected_findings.rule: 21 U.S.C. 352(n); 21 CFR 202.1(e)(1) (broadcast major statement); FTC Act §§5, 12

expected_findings.claim: See Important Safety Information about GLP-1 medications, including Boxed Warning, at ro.co/safety. GLP-1 medications may have serious side effects. Do not use if you or your family have a history of a type of thyroid cancer called MTC or MEN2. In rodents, they cause thyroid C-Cell tumors and their impact in humans is not known.
expected_findings.rule: 21 CFR 202.1(e)(1), (e)(7)(viii); FTC Act §5 (clear and conspicuous; 16 CFR 255.0(f))

expected_findings.claim: Joint Stress Reduced (on-screen graphic over knee) with VO "I'm moving better on Ro"
Blood Sugar Steady (on-screen graphic) with VO "I'm feeling better on Ro"

must_not_flag: "34 lbs down on GLP-1s" / "↓34lbs GLP-1 journey in a year" (00:02-00:07) is accompanied by a generally-expected-results disclosure: "Average weight loss with GLP-1s is 14-20% in 1 year, when paired with diet and exercise." plus source footnote ("Based on manufacturer trials studying the highest doses of FDA-approved GLP-1 medications...") (~00:03-00:09) - do not flag as misleading_testimonial_or_results
"FDA approved GLP-1 options. Now even in a pill." (00:11-00:16) - refers to branded FDA-approved GLP-1s; do not flag as false_fda_approval_claim
On-screen indication statement "GLP-1 medications through Ro are prescribed for obesity or overweight." (~00:19-00:21)

"Monthly subscription required and excludes medication. Ro does not provide medical services, but connects you with an independent, licensed healthcare professional who will prescribe medication, if right for you. Not available in all states." (~00:23-00:28) - business-model disclosure
Serena Williams appearing as an endorser (no evidence in the asset that she is not a real user)
notes: Provenance: official 'Ro' YouTube channel, uploaded 2026-01-28; Super Bowl LX spot. Captions = YouTube auto-captions (they render 'Ro' as 'row'; corrected in ad_content). Fine print read from a 1080p copy (480p copy kept as asset; fine print is barely legible at 480p). Labels by agent from captions+frames; needs human confirmation. Verdict is needs_review because the ad names a drug class ('GLP-1s', 'FDA approved GLP-1 options... in a pill') but no specific product, so whether 21 CFR 202.1 broadcast major-statement rules apply to Ro (a telehealth platform, not the manufacturer) is a legal judgment; benefits are in audio while risk info is on-screen only for ~5s. The knee/glucose graphics are qualified by an on-screen footnote ("In clinical trials, patients who lost weight saw lowered glucose levels and reported improvement in knee joint pain."); whether these are off-label for the specific products prescribed needs a reviewer with current labeling. Context: Managed Healthcare Executive noted "Williams does not refer to a particular GLP-1, which explains the lack of a disclaimer about side effects" (https://www.managedhealthcareexecutive.com/view/wegovy-uacr-test-spotlighted-in-the-health-oriented-super-bowl-ads). No FDA action specific to this ad was found.

title: Megan Fox is Ro Sparks | Ro Sparks TV Commercial (2026)
ad_content: [00:00] Hi, I'm not Viagra. [00:02] I'm Ro Sparks, a prescription medication for men. [00:05] My dual action formula includes sildenafil, [00:08] the active ingredient in Viagra. [00:10] Plus, tadalafil, so I stay in your system, [00:12] ready to go for up to 36 hours. [00:15] I dissolve under your tongue, that's for speed. [00:17] And tadalafil lasts for hours and hours. [00:20] If prescribed, I show up right at your door. [00:23] Don't worry, my packaging is very discreet. [00:26] I'm Megan Fox. [00:28] This is Ro Sparks.

expected_findings.claim: My dual action formula includes sildenafil ... Plus, tadalafil, so I stay in your system, ready to go for up to 36 hours. I dissolve under your tongue, that's for speed.
expected_findings.rule: 21 U.S.C. 352(n); 21 CFR 202.1(e)(1) (broadcast major statement); FTC Act §§5, 12

expected_findings.claim: Hi, I'm not Viagra. ... My dual action formula includes sildenafil, the active ingredient in Viagra.
Plus, tadalafil, so I stay in your system, ready to go for up to 36 hours. ... And tadalafil lasts for hours and hours.
expected_findings.rule: 21 U.S.C. 352(a); 21 CFR 202.1(e)(6); FTC Act §§5, 12 (competent and reliable scientific evidence)

expected_findings.claim: Sublingual formulations dissolve under the tongue so the medication hits the bloodstream faster than pills. (VO: "I dissolve under your tongue, that's for speed.")
Ro Sparks is a compounded drug, which may be prescribed under federal law, but is not FDA-approved and does not undergo FDA safety or effectiveness review.
expected_findings.rule: FTC Act §5 (clear and conspicuous; 16 CFR 255.0(f) - disclosure in at least the same means as the triggering claim); 21 CFR 202.1(e)(1)

must_not_flag: No claim that Ro Sparks is FDA-approved; the ad states it is not - do not raise false_fda_approval_claim
"Prescription treatment for men, if eligible." (~00:10-00:14) and "If prescribed, I show up right at your door." (00:20-00:23) - accurate Rx/eligibility qualifiers
"Don't worry, my packaging is very discreet." (00:23-00:26) - logistics claim, not a health claim
"To be very clear, you cannot order Megan Fox on Ro." (end card) - humorous disclaimer
Megan Fox personifies the product; she is not presented as a patient testimonial - do not flag as misleading_testimonial_or_results
notes: Provenance: official 'Ro' YouTube channel, uploaded 2026-10-01. No YouTube captions were available; transcript produced locally with Whisper (mlx-community/whisper-small.en-mlx). ASR errors corrected: 'Rose Sparks' -> 'Ro Sparks' (matches on-screen brand), 'todalafil' -> 'tadalafil'. Fine print read from a 1080p copy. Labels by agent from captions+frames; needs human confirmation. On-screen timing: compounded/not-FDA-approved single-line super ~0-10.3s; 'Prescription treatment for men, if eligible.' ~10.3-14s; sublingual 'faster than pills' super ~16-21.5s; end card ~24.3-30s: 'Connect with a licensed provider online to see if you're eligible. For Important Safety Information, visit ro.co/safetyinfo' + 5-line paragraph incl. 'This is a compounded drug product. Compounded drugs ... are not FDA-approved and do not undergo FDA safety, effectiveness, or manufacturing review.' No risk statement (e.g., nitrate contraindication) appears in audio or on screen; only a URL reference. Context: Adweek describes Ro Sparks as Ro's compounded 'fast-acting erectile dysfunction pill' that is 'not approved by the FDA' (https://www.adweek.com/brand-marketing/megan-fox-is-the-ed-treatment-in-new-ro-sparks-campaign/). The 'active ingredient in Viagra' framing parallels the 'same active ingredient' claims FDA objected to in its Sept 9, 2025 warning letter to Hims & Hers (https://spectrumlocalnews.com/us/snplus/health/2025/09/16/fda-takes-aim-at-hims---hers--weight-loss-drugs-in-ad-blitz); no FDA action specific to this ad was found.

title: Keeps Hair Loss Commercial — "No More Covering Up"
ad_content: [00:00] Cover it up, that's what I did when I started losing my hair. [00:04] Now I use Keeps, the easiest way for me to keep my hair. [00:07] Keeps sends me clinically proven treatments that can stop my hair loss, [00:11] which means no more covering up. [00:13] Go to keeps.com to learn more.
must_not_flag: "Keeps sends me clinically proven treatments that can stop my hair loss" (00:07-00:13) - hedged ('can'); finasteride and minoxidil are FDA-approved for male pattern hair loss
End-card package text "Men's Extra Strength Hair Regrowth Treatment" / "Clinically Proven To Help Regrow Hair" / "Not for use by women" (00:13-00:15) - OTC minoxidil package labeling
"the easiest way for me to keep my hair" (00:04-00:07) - subjective consumer opinion
No specific prescription drug is named, no quantified results, no FDA-approval or comparative claims
notes: Provenance: official 'Keeps' YouTube channel, uploaded 2018-12-10 (pre-dates the 2023 FTC Endorsement Guides revision). Captions = YouTube auto-captions. Labels by agent from captions+frames; needs human confirmation. Included as a compliant control. Borderline points a human should confirm: (1) consumer endorser testimonial with only 'Individual results may vary.' as a qualifier; (2) an unlabeled Rx-style pill bottle appears on the end card next to the OTC minoxidil box, with no risk information - acceptable only if the ad is treated as a service/brand ad that names no Rx drug. No regulatory action or news criticism found for this specific ad.
